Manawa Ora Mirimiri - The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork WELLINGTON
OUR LAST EVENT FOR 2026

Nau mai, haere mai ki Manawa Ora – The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork.

Experience traditional Māori healing practices grounded in cultural knowledge in this 2-day Foundational workshop with Manawa Ora.

We invite you to reconnect with the wisdom of our tūpuna and explore the foundations of traditional Māori healing through a holistic, hands-on approach to wellbeing. Grounded in mātauranga Māori, this workshop provides an introduction to the principles, values and practices that underpin Māori healing.

Throughout this workshop, participants will be introduced to mirimiri and romiromi (Māori bodywork), exploring intention and connection in the healing process. We will consider cultural aspects such as whakapapa, tikanga, manaakitanga and wairuatanga.

The workshop offers a supportive space to learn, reflect and develop an awareness of how Māori healing traditions can inform our approach to wellbeing, both for ourselves and for those we care for. Participants will be encouraged to pay attention to their own bodies, deepen their connection with others and appreciate the responsibility that comes with engaging in the healing process.

Over the last 10 years, these workshops have welcomed people from all races and backgrounds. Wānanga/workshops are safe spaces for people to come together for the pupose of learning and healing, guided by tikanga.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

Whether you are beginning your journey into Māori healing or seeking to strengthen your existing understanding, this workshop provides a foundation from which to grow with respect, aroha and intention.

PLEASE NOTE THIS WORKSHOP IS NOT A QUALIFICATION TO PRACTICE.

The 2-day workshop includes:
- Cultural philosophies
- Whatumanawa (intuitive diagnosis)
- Self-awareness and insight
- Waiata, karakia and takutaku
- Spiritual hygiene
- Introduction to mirimiri and romiromi
- Group interaction & hands-on practice
- Selfcare and tools to maintain wellness

Facilitator Jolie Davis has over 30 years experience in Rongoā Māori; mirimiri and romiromi. Educator, advocate, founder and lead practitioner at Manawa Ora; the largest provider of Rongoā Māori in the Wellington region.

WHO THIS WĀNANGA IS FOR:
This wānanga welcomes all with an open heart and an open mind
Individuals on a personal healing journey, ready to discover their inner potential.
- Māori seeking reconnection with whakapapa, culture and self-identity.
- Those drawn to indigenous healing modalities and philosophy.
- Bodyworkers, healers and mainstream practitioners seeking to expand their knowledge and enrich their practice.

Our venue is Manawa Ora whare hauora (clinic), 236 Middleton Rd, Glenside, WELLINGTON.

long_description:
WELLINGTON INTERNATIONAL UKULELE ORCHESTRA 2027
After ten years in ‘deep hibernation’, the much-loved Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra (WIUO) will reassemble for a spectacular show at the newly restored Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall on Saturday 20 March 2027.

This special event reunites two treasured Wellington icons, both relishing being back in action, with stronger foundations, sexier décor and refreshed acoustics.

Founded a bit by accident in 2005 by friends Age Pryor (The Woolshed Sessions, Congress of Animals, Fly My Pretties) and Bret McKenzie (Flight of the Conchords, The Black Seeds), what began as a joyful experiment quickly evolved into one of New Zealand's most celebrated live acts.

Over the following decade, the Orchestra captivated audiences throughout Aotearoa and around the world, releasing four bestselling EPs and an album, collaborating with internationally renowned artists, and inspiring thousands of people to discover the joy of making music.

Following an extensive touring schedule that included New Zealand, Australia, UK, the United States, China and Japan, the band put their ukes on ice to explore other instruments and new creative pursuits.

But the call of the ukulele is strong - asked if they’d regroup for one special all-ages show to celebrate Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall’s triumphant reopening, the Orchestra’s answer was an instant “holy hecking ukeballs YES”.

The band said: "That's what it's always been about for us: getting everyone together, lifting the roof and finding magic in the moment through amazing music."

The reunion feels especially fitting for a group that sprang from the creative milieu of mid-2000s Te Whanganui-a-Tara. The Town Hall, City Gallery, Central Library and Michael Fowler Centre all formed part of the Orchestra's journey as it grew from local curiosity to international phenomenon.

Heidi Morton, GM Events & Experiences at WellingtonNZ, says: "The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra holds a special place in Wellington's cultural story, and we're delighted to welcome them back as part of the celebrations marking the reopening of Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. We know many people will be eager to join in for this one – so be sure to get your tickets quickly as we definitely expect a sell-out.”

Audiences can expect everything they remember and love about the WIUO: soaring harmonies, dazzling musicianship, inventive arrangements, spontaneous comedy and plenty of audience participation. The performance will feature beloved classics, new material and, inevitably, a few trademark surprises.

The band’s repertoire takes a gloriously democratic approach to the global songbook, moving seamlessly between pop hits, rock classics, country ballads, waiata Māori and Pacific, indie treasures and unexpected deep cuts. Proud champions of the unique instrument and its surprising range, the WIUO proves that a room full of ukuleles can be moving, virtuosic, funny and unexpectedly powerful, often all in the same song.

The first rule of the Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra remains unchanged: “If you know the words, sing along.” And the second: “If you don’t know the words, sing along.”

The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra also features Andy Morley-Hall, Bek Coogan, Carmel Russell, Daniel Yeabsley, Deanne Krieg, Francis Salole, Gemma Gracewood, Megan Salole, Nigel Collins, Samuel Auger and Stephen Jessup.

Presented by Venues Wellington’s Live in WLG, this special reunion celebrates not only the return of the Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra, but also the reopening of a venue that has long been at the heart of the capital's cultural life.

For one night only, Wellingtonians and visitors will once again have the chance to gather and celebrate together in one of the city's most treasured communal spaces.

long_description:
[FREE] Michael Volkerling Memorial Lecture: Artificial Intelligence, Memory and Culture
Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are already embedded in the communication of culture – they shape and touch on all aspects of culture. In the face of this, an intense debate is currently taking place in museums around the world: are AI technologies to be embraced and trusted or should they be approached with suspicion and resisted?

This lecture attempts to unpick this dilemma by drawing on contemporary examples of AI use in heritage practices, in and beyond the museum. The lecture critically reflects on the opportunities and challenges of AI technologies and ‘synthetic’ media for memory institutions, the knowledges they care for and their audiences. It further asks what kind of ethics and institutional futures museums should strive for when attempting to navigate this fast-evolving techno-cultural environment.

Professor Areti Galani is Deputy Head in the School of Arts and Cultures, at Newcastle University, UK. Areti has led theoretical, empirical and creative practice-based research on digital imaginaries of European heritage and she is a lead editor/author of the volume European Heritage, Dialogue and Digital Practices (Routledge, 2019). She is currently a co-investigator in the project Living Cultural Labs (LIL-ECHOES, 2026-30), which explores how virtual worlds and AI-enabled cultural environments can help Europe turn cultural difference into a shared resource for belonging.

This free public lecture marks the legacy of the late Dr Michael Volkerling, former Chief Executive of the Museum of New Zealand, who made a huge contribution to the local cultural heritage sector over 30 years. This event is presented in partnership with National Services Te Paerangi and the Stout Research Centre.

The lecture will be recorded and made available on the National Services Te Paerangi website following the event.

Terror of the Deep Album Release! with Spirit Level
To celebrate the fifteenth anniversary of its initial release, Terror of the Deep are proud to present their sophomore album ‘Permanent Weekend’.

From the viscous psych-rock of Airport Underneath the Dome to the lavish, prog-rock inspired Space Epic, Terror Of The Deep have charted the depths of our oceans and the outer reaches of our solar system with a dedicated following in NZ and overseas. Consisting of Taipua Adams (bass), William Daymond (drums), Tom Watson (keys) and Oliver Dixon (guitar and lead vocal), the band were named by New York-based culture website Flavourwire as one of the ‘10 Great New Zealand Bands You Should Know’. To celebrate the fifteenth anniversary of its initial release, Terror of the Deep are proud to present their sophomore album ‘Permanent Weekend’ on limited-edition, hand numbered vinyl. Pressed at Mobineko in Taiwan on 140gm black vinyl, the original 11 song album has been given a fresh remaster and a new running order for this release. Each copy also contains a full colour insert featuring photos, posters, set lists, and reviews from when the album was first released in October 2011. LPs will be available to purchase at the gig.
-
Spirit Level is a new duo of long time sonic voyagers, Daniel Beban (guitar) and Andy Wright (drums). Plucking notes from the void, Dan employs an electric 12-string through a vintage Italian echo device and two classic NZ amps, creating crystalline layers of shifting harmonies and frozen peals of bell-like melodies that hover over Andy's playfully intricate summoning of interstellar energy.

Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

long_description:
In person Motu Seminar: Global shifts in the labour market and NZ
An in-person Motu Public Policy Seminar on global shifts in the labour market and what they could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand

About this Event



Join us for a Motu Research (with support from The Treasury New Zealand) public policy seminar on "Global shifts in the labour market and what they could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand".

We have four speakers with expertise in labour markets (Alexander Hijzen, OECD; Dr Lisa Meehan, Director, New Zealand Policy Research Institute; Christopher Ball, RBNZ; and Amanda Reid, CEO of BERL). Their presentations will be followed by audience questions.

You can attend this seminar either in person or online. We will provide the recording and slides afterwards.

For in person participants - please allow yourself time to sign in at The Treasury reception (level 3, 1 The Terrace). Morning tea is available at the venue from 10am.

Motu Research seminars bring expert research into conversation with policy makers, researchers and other stakeholders. Speakers present their findings, then take questions from a panel and the audience. Recent seminars have covered Treasury's social discount rate, children's development, and public housing and wellbeing. You can see recordings of our past seminars here.

When: 17 November from 10.30am-12pm (if attending in person, morning tea served from 10am).

Where: The Treasury seminar room, 1 The Terrace, Wellington AND on online.


Video call details for online participants:
Microsoft Teams meeting
Join: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/411230592011907?p=LzPaskP44f1CqcwCCU
Meeting ID: 411 230 592 011 907
Passcode: nk2hV9NW


About the speakers

Alexander Hijzen, OECD is a senior economist at the Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs of the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD), the project leader of the OECD LinkEED 2.0 network and a Research Fellow of IZA@LISER. He has previously worked at the International Monetary Fund and the Centre for Research on Globalisation and Economic Policy (GEP) at the University of Nottingham. His research has been published in international academic journals. Alexander holds a Ph.D. in Economics from the University of Nottingham and is of Dutch citizenship. He has worked on job mobility, labour reallocation, ageing and productivity. He works on income distribution and labour economics more broadly. Alexander will speak about two chapters in the recent OECD analysis called . The chapters are “Reviving growth in an ageing world: The role of job mobility”, that includes Aotearoa New Zealand - and “Places and people: The impact of structural change on local labour markets”.

Dr Lisa Meehan, Director, New Zealand Policy Research Institute, Auckland University of Technology. Lisa is an applied economist with extensive experience in economic research and public policy, having previously worked at the OECD, the New Zealand Productivity Commission and the New Zealand Treasury. Her research focuses on labour markets, productivity, education, health, workforce diversity and inequality. She is particularly interested in how technological change (including artificial intelligence) may affect skills development, employment opportunities and labour market inequality. She has recently worked on productivity growth, New Zealand’s labour income share, and broader shifts in labour markets.

Christopher Ball, RBNZ is a Senior Advisor in the Research and Analytics team at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. His recent work includes research on job-to-job mobility in New Zealand and the exposure of the New Zealand labour market to artificial intelligence and robotics.

Amanda Reid, CEO of BERL, whose work spans labour market trends, workforce development, and future workforce challenges in Aotearoa New Zealand. She will speak on the labour market impacts of AI, and technology more broadly, particularly what these shifts could mean for young people.

Motu Public Policy Seminars are free to the public, but please to receive email notifications of Motu Research's events and publications.

Thanks to The Treasury NZ and Russell McVeagh for their generous support of our seminars.

Tickets on sale Monday 2nd November 6pm via Humanitix.

Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK.
Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...
UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'
MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’
Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’
MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.
AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

BIMinNZ Wellington - Project Spotlight - Air NZ Hangar 4
Join us in Wellington to hear from the design and construction teams that brought this innovative project to life.

About this Event



Join us on 17 November at Tonkin + Taylor for our final BIMinNZ Wellington event of 2026, as we explore the technology, innovation and collaboration behind Air New Zealand's remarkable new Hangar 4 project.

Designed by Studio Pacific Architecture and constructed by NZ Strong, Hangar 4 is the Southern Hemisphere's largest single span timber aircraft hangar. This impressive 15,000m² facility features a 98 metre clear span, enormous prefabricated timber trusses weighing 38 tonnes each, and an innovative approach to sustainable construction that sets a new benchmark for aviation infrastructure.

We'll be joined by Patrick Thompson from Studio Pacific Architecture and Jimmy Corric from NZ Strong, who will take us behind the scenes of this extraordinary project, exploring the digital tools, innovative construction methodologies and collaborative processes that helped bring it to life.

From complex design coordination and prefabrication to the challenges of construction within an operational airport environment, this session promises valuable insights into how technology and innovation are helping deliver some of New Zealand's most ambitious projects.

Come along to connect with Wellington's digital built environment community, hear from the people behind this impressive project, and celebrate another fantastic year of BIMinNZ events!

Arturo Báez (Mexico) Performance Residency - Night 1
We are very happy to present the wonderful Mexican double bassist Arturo Báez for two nights, playing solo and in improvised collaborations with a host of top notch local musicians.


Arturo Báez Velázquez is a Mexican double bassist and electric bassist whose music moves between jazz, free improvisation and spontaneous collective creation. Báez was born in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán. He began playing folkloric music of the region at the age of 14, and moved to Mexico City at 19 to pursue his musical studies.

For more than 15 years, he has been an active presence in Mexico’s improvised music scene, collaborating with internationally acclaimed artists including Ken Vandermark, Joe Morris, Chris Corsano, Michael Zerang, Sam Newsome, Isaiah Collier, Dennis Gonzalez, Blaise Siwula, Brian Allen, Leo Genovese, David Borgo, Linda Briceño, Justo Almario, Víctor Mendoza, Remi Álvarez, Cristóbal López, Héctor Infanzón, Gabriel Puentes and Alejandro Campos, among others.

A prolific artist, Arturo is a regular member of many projects including Big Band Jazz de México, the Remi Álvarez Trío, Chocolate Smoke Gang, Carlos Marx and the Jorge Fernández Project. His international work includes performances at the No Idea Festival in Austin and across the United States, Europe and Asia. He leads Otrora un Simulacro, a creative jazz ensemble that features his original compositions.

long_description:
Whitireia Park Community Snorkel - FREE
Dive in with us this summer! 🌊

Discover the underwater world of Whitireia Park at our free community snorkelling event! Explore beautiful seagrass beds, rocky reefs and the marine life that calls them home — you might even spot a seahorse!

🐠 Everyone welcome, including beginners!

We provide all the snorkelling gear and experienced guides to help you enjoy a safe and memorable experience in the water.

A few things to know:

Participants must be aged 8+ and confident swimmers.

Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult who also takes part in the snorkel.

Bring your togs, towel, refreshments and anything else you need to enjoy a day by the coast.

🤿 How to take part

Registrations open at 9.45am on the day. Come along to book your snorkel time — spots may fill up quickly!

Each tour takes approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes, including getting ready, snorkelling and returning your gear afterwards. The last tour departs at 1.45pm.

Make a day of it and enjoy exploring the coast and taking part in other activities!

This free event is brought to you in partnership with Greater Wellington Regional Council.

📍 Getting there

By bike: Why not enjoy the beautiful coastal track? It's approximately 5km from Titahi Bay Boat Club to the snorkel site.

By car: The road to the snorkel site is narrow and can be challenging when traffic is busy. Where possible, please carpool and drive carefully. Clearly signposted parking will be available throughout the day.


🌦️ Weather and event updates

Snorkelling is weather-dependent, and events may be cancelled, postponed or moved to another location. Please check this Mountains to Sea Wellington Facebook event listing for updates before heading out.

................................................................................................................................

This snorkelling event is delivered under the national Mountains to Sea Conservation Trust's Experiencing Marine Reserves programme.

The programme is Adventure Activity Certified (AA0534).
